home.howTitle: How the contrast ratio is calculated
home.howIntro: WCAG defines contrast using **relative luminance**, how bright a color appears to the human eye on a scale from 0 (black) to 1 (white). For each color, ContrastCheck:
howSteps: Splits the hex value into red, green and blue channels and divides each by 255.
Linearizes each channel: values ≤ 0.04045 are divided by 12.92; otherwise `((c + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4`.
Weights them by how sensitive our eyes are to each: `L = 0.2126·R + 0.7152·G + 0.0722·B`.
home.howRatio: The contrast ratio is then `(L_lighter + 0.05) / (L_darker + 0.05)`, which ranges from 1:1 for identical colors to 21:1 for black on white. The result is compared to the thresholds without rounding: 4.5:1 (AA) and 7:1 (AAA) for normal text, 3:1 (AA) and 4.5:1 (AAA) for large text, and 3:1 for UI components and graphics.

faq.q: What is a good color contrast ratio?
faq.a: WCAG 2.2 Level AA requires at least 4.5:1 for normal body text and 3:1 for large text. Level AAA raises that to 7:1 for normal text and 4.5:1 for large text. Ratios range from 1:1 (identical colors) to 21:1 (black on white).

faq.q: What counts as large text in WCAG?
faq.a: Large text is at least 18 point (about 24 CSS px) at regular weight, or at least 14 point (about 18.66 CSS px) when bold. Large text has lower contrast thresholds because bigger glyphs are easier to read.

faq.q: What is the 3:1 UI component and graphics requirement?
faq.a: WCAG success criterion 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast requires a 3:1 ratio for the visual boundaries of interactive controls (input borders, focus rings, toggle states) and for graphical objects such as icons and chart lines needed to understand content.

faq.q: Does the order of foreground and background matter?
faq.a: No. The WCAG formula always divides the lighter color's luminance by the darker one's, so swapping foreground and background gives the same ratio. The preview changes, but the numbers and pass/fail results do not.
No. This color contrast checker runs entirely in your browser. The only place your colors are stored is the page URL (?fg=…&bg=…), which lets you bookmark or share a specific pair.

faq.q: Why does 4.49:1 fail when it is so close to 4.5:1?
faq.a: WCAG thresholds are hard minimums and are not rounded. ContrastCheck compares the exact ratio and truncates the displayed value, so a pair that shows 4.49:1 fails AA for normal text. Use the suggested color to nudge it over the line.

faq.q: Does this checker support APCA or WCAG 3?
faq.a: Not yet. ContrastCheck uses the WCAG 2.x contrast ratio, which is what current laws and procurement standards (ADA guidance, Section 508, EN 301 549 / European Accessibility Act) reference today.

guide.headline: WCAG AA vs AAA Contrast: Which Level Should You Target?
guide.intro: WCAG 2.2 defines two levels of text contrast. **AA** is the level referenced by most accessibility laws and policies; **AAA** is an enhanced level for content that needs to be readable by as many people as possible.
guide.criteria: The text criteria are SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) for AA and SC 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced) for AAA. Logos, purely decorative text and disabled controls are exempt.
guide.largeBody: WCAG defines large text as at least **18 point** regular or **14 point bold**. On the web, 1pt = 1.333px, so that is roughly **24px** regular or **18.66px** bold. Most body copy (14–18px) is _normal_ text and needs the stricter threshold.
guide.examplesHint: Click any example to open it in the checker.

advice.title: Aim for AA everywhere.
advice.text: ADA guidance in the US, Section 508, EN 301 549 and the European Accessibility Act all point to WCAG Level AA. Failing AA is a real compliance risk.

advice.title: Use AAA for long-form reading.
advice.text: Articles, documentation, government and healthcare content benefit from 7:1 body text, especially for older readers and people with low vision.

advice.title: Don’t require AAA site-wide.
advice.text: W3C itself notes that AAA cannot be met for all content. Treat it as a goal for primary text, not a blocker for brand colors on large headings.

advice.title: Don’t forget non-text contrast.
advice.text: Input borders, focus indicators and icons that convey meaning need 3:1 against adjacent colors, even if your text passes.
